cues: The way round it is to take both beams from a single source.
Then whatever random phase jump happens, happens in both beams at once, and cancels out of the phase difference.
Division of wavefront: use two parts of the same wavefront, as in Young's double slit.
Division of amplitude: split one beam by partial reflection, as in a soap bubble, or the rainbow colours of oil on a wet road.
And lasers are naturally coherent, which makes all this easy.
text: The way round it is to take both beams from a single source. Then whatever random phase jump happens, happens in both beams at once, and cancels out of the phase difference. There are two ways. Division of wavefront: use two parts of the same wavefront, as in Young's double slit. Division of amplitude: split one beam by partial reflection, as in a soap bubble, or the rainbow colours of oil on a wet road. And lasers are naturally coherent, which makes all this easy.
